relevance_note: Cohort study of 4 sibling pairs with GAMT deficiency with per-sibling sex, age and treatment in Table 1: "4 sibling pairs with GAMT-D (n = 8, age range 9.0–18.7 years, 4 male, 4 female)".
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a short script assembled the JSON and checked spans. Table 1 has families as rows ('Case 1'-'Case 4') and siblings as column pairs headed 'Younger'/'Older' (row '| Sibling | Younger | Older |'); each sibling is labelled '<Younger|Older> (Family <n>)' with n the Table 1 Case number, since the same column label recurs in four families. Sex/age spans quote the Case row from its label through the sibling's cell (Sex, Age [y], Start treatment [y], Treatment column pairs: first = Younger, second = Older). The 16 healthy control siblings are out of scope (no rows); cohort_size_as_stated = 8 GAMT-D patients (controls are not patients; no total of 24 is stated). No variant rows: the paper states 'Genetic variant information was not collected' and ties no printed GAMT variant to any person. Prior reports are hedged ('may have been reported on'); recorded as true with the families and reference numbers verbatim. Individuals are identified in the text only through Table 1 attributes (treatment at 3.9 years = Younger Case 4; diagnosed and treated at 0.8 years = Older Case 2) or as named groups ('older case group', 'younger case group'). Quotes tagged '(family n)' in the text are attributed to Table 1 Case n only for families 1 and 4, where the text matches Table 1 (family 1: older daughter diagnosed at 5.5 years vs Case 1 older female starting treatment at 5.6 y; family 4: daughter 14 y, son 9 y = Case 4 ages). The paper never states that text 'family n' equals Table 1 'Case n'; for families 2 and 3 the match is doubtful (the family 3 son is 'age 16' but Case 3 older is 18.3 y, Case 2 older 16.0 y), so their quotes (motor, speech, therapy) were not attributed to anyone. Group counts without names (self-harming in 2 of 4 older, 3 of 4 older still with refractory seizures, therapies counts) were not assigned to anyone. 'No behavioral abnormalities were reported for the younger sibling in the case group' was not used to exclude behaviours (wording is 'not reported'). 'Learning difficulties or learning disabilities' was not mapped to the developmental delay/intellectual disability checklist item except for Older (Family 4), whose parent describes a severe learning disability with function 'more like a 5 years old' at 14 years. Ages in Table 1 are years at participation; treatment start ages are recorded in treatment_summary, not as diagnosis ages. Contradictions: none found beyond the family 3 age mismatch noted above.
